newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Van Eck fund favors Hong Kong's "red chips".
newsitem.headline: U.S. Van Eck fund favors Hong Kong's "red chips".

text.p: The neckbreaking pace of initial public offerings of red chips and the phenomenal gains of those shares are transforming the Hong Kong stock market, injecting new energy in an already vibrant market, said Jan van Eck, emerging market strategist at Van Eck Global Funds.
"There are really two stock markets in Hong Kong: Hong Kong blue chips and 'Greater China' stocks," van Eck told a media luncheon at the fund's headquarters on Thursday.
"Investing in red chips is a direct play on China's (economic) growth," he said.
Red chips are companies that are registered in Hong Kong, but have mainland China parents.
Admitting that Red chips are not all efficient companies, van Eck expected the companies would make large strides after Hong Kong's return to Chinese sovereignty.
"Hong Kong provides a regulatory structure and these companies can pick up management skills (from Hong Kong)," he said.

After Hong Kong's return to China, the new government is likely to come under strong societal pressure to ease the housing shortage, which could bring short-term volatility to the properties market, which accounts for one-third of the value of the Hang Seng stock market index, said Kevin Reid, a portfolio manager at Van Eck Securities. But in the long run, more affordable housing should bring greater economic benefit to Hong Kong, he said.
